source_text: Ut sine dono diaboli, ad quod dicis libidinem sexuum pertinere, nuptiae, quas Deus creaverat, esse non possent; immo illis, quas ordinaverat, institutionis suae honore avolantibus, has, quarum ordo permansit, cum motione genitalium, cum pudore coeuntium, cum calore et consternatione membrorum, cum iucunditate sensuum, cum iniquitate nascentium, diaboli, non Dei opus esse cogeret atque convinceret.
pass_a_gloss: So that without the devil's gift, to which you say the lust of the sexes belongs, marriages, which God had created, could not be; nay, those which he had ordained flying away with the honor of his institution, he would force and convict these, whose order remained, with the motion of the genitals, with the modesty of those coupling, with the heat and prostration of the members, with the pleasantness of the senses, with the iniquity of those being born, to be a work of the devil, not of God.

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise not a nature-sin substance
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: —so that marriage, which God had created, could not exist without the devil’s gift, to which you assign sexual desire; or rather, so that the marriages God had ordained flew away with the honor of his institution, and Adam forced and proved the marriages whose order remained to be the devil’s work, not God’s, with their genital movement, the partners’ modesty, the heat and agitation of their limbs, the delight of their senses, and the guilt of their newborn children—

choices.why: Julian refuses to make marital desire a nature-sin substance planted by the devil.
Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
